questions.q: You are riding your motorcycle straight ahead on a main road. Whom must you give way to?
options: Only the tram
Only the white car
The tram and the white car
No one
questions.explain: The tram is approaching along a minor road (sign 2.4). At an intersection of roads of unequal status, the driver on the minor road gives way, and this includes a tram. The white car is turning left from the opposite direction and gives way to you.

questions.q: You and the oncoming traffic have a green light. You are riding straight ahead on your motorcycle, and an oncoming white car is turning left. What is the best thing to do?
options: Go first, but slow down and be ready to brake
Go without reducing speed: you have priority
Stop and let the white car through
Sound the horn and accelerate to get through
questions.explain: When turning left on a green light, the driver of the white car must give way to you ⟦66⟧. But cars turning left in front of a motorcyclist are one of the main dangers: drivers often do not notice the motorcycle. So reduce speed and be ready to brake.

questions.q: There is a dangerous bend ahead. How should you take it on a motorcycle?
options: Enter the bend at your previous speed and brake in the bend
Reduce speed before the bend and look where you want to go
In the bend, look at the front wheel and the road markings
Pull in the clutch and coast through the whole bend
questions.explain: Sign 1.11.1, the “Dangerous bend to the right” sign, warns of a bend of small radius or with restricted view. You reduce speed before the bend by closing the throttle and, if necessary, applying both brakes, and in the bend you look where you want to go. Entering too fast carries the motorcycle into the oncoming lane or off the road.

questions.q: You are already taking a bend on your motorcycle when an obstruction suddenly appears ahead in your lane. What is the best way to stop?
options: Brake hard with the front brake without straightening the motorcycle
Lock the rear wheel and turn the motorcycle sideways
First straighten the motorcycle, then brake
Pull in the clutch and drive round the obstruction without braking
questions.explain: Hard braking while leaning easily makes the wheels lose grip. The motorcyclists' manual names as the best technique to straighten the motorcycle first and then brake. If you have to brake while leaning, you brake gently and reduce the lean as your speed falls.

questions.q: Which brake gives a motorcycle most of its braking force?
options: The rear: about two thirds
Both equally, half each
Engine braking: more than half
The front: at least three quarters
questions.explain: When braking, the weight of the motorcycle shifts to the front wheel, so the front brake is more powerful: it provides at least three quarters of the total braking force. To stop, you use both brakes at the same time.

questions.q: You need to stop quickly on a straight, dry road. How do you brake on a motorcycle?
options: Apply both brakes at once, without “grabbing” the front one
Only the rear brake, without touching the front
Only the front brake, sharply, until the wheel locks
Pull in the clutch and coast to a stop
questions.explain: To stop quickly you apply both brakes at the same time. Do not be afraid to use the front brake, but apply it smoothly and firmly, not with a jerk.

questions.q: The front wheel locks while you are braking. What should you do?
options: Hold the brake until the motorcycle stops completely
Release the front brake at once and apply it again
Open the throttle so that the wheel starts turning again
Turn the handlebars sharply in the direction the motorcycle is leaning
questions.explain: A locked front wheel does not hold its direction, and the motorcycle falls. The motorcyclists' manual advises releasing the front brake at once and then applying it again firmly.

questions.q: You need to swerve sharply round an obstruction. When should you brake?
options: During the swerve
Only after the engine has stopped
Before or after the swerve, but not during it
At the same time as turning the handlebars: it is quicker
questions.explain: During a sharp swerve the motorcycle leans, and braking may make the wheels lose grip. So you brake before the manoeuvre or after it.

questions.q: When is the asphalt especially slippery for a motorcycle?
options: An hour after the rain starts, when the oil has already been washed off
In dry, cool weather in the daytime
In the first minutes of rain, before the oil is washed off
At night in dry, windless weather
questions.explain: Right after the rain starts, the water mixes with the oil and dust on the asphalt, and the surface becomes especially slippery. Later the rain washes the oil to the edges of the road.

questions.q: Which places on a wet road are especially dangerous for a motorcycle?
options: The middle of the lane, with smooth, clean asphalt
Dry sections under bridges and overpasses
Places where the asphalt is rough and there are no puddles
Road markings, metal plates and manhole covers
questions.explain: In the rain, the paint of road markings and the metal of manhole covers and plates become very slippery. Wet leaves, sand and gravel at the edge of the road are also dangerous.

questions.q: How should you cross tram rails, ruts or longitudinal joints in the road surface on a motorcycle?
options: Along the rail, so that the wheel follows the groove
At any angle, if your speed is high
At an angle of at least 45 degrees
Only standing on the footrests
questions.explain: If you cross rails or a rut at a shallow angle, the wheel may drop into the groove and the motorcycle will fall. The motorcyclists' manual advises moving over and crossing them at an angle of at least 45 degrees.

questions.q: What is the minimum following distance to the vehicle ahead that a motorcyclist is advised to keep?
options: Half a second
1 metre
The length of one motorcycle
2 seconds
questions.explain: The Rules require a following distance that lets you avoid a collision. The motorcyclists' manual gives the usual minimum as 2 seconds.

questions.q: At the test, in the “Dimensional figure eight” exercise, you touched the ground with your foot. What will be the result?
options: 100 penalty points: the test is failed
5 penalty points: it is only a remark
25 penalty points: you may continue
10 penalty points for each touch
questions.explain: Under the autodrome methodology, touching the surface of the test area with a foot in the motorcycle exercises gives 100 penalty points. The result “fail” is given if more than 99 points are scored, that is, for a single such touch.

questions.q: What must you do at the category A test before the “Start” command?
options: Fasten the helmet, switch on the hazard warning lights and the main beam
Fasten the helmet, adjust the mirrors, switch on the dipped headlight
Take off the helmet to hear the commands better, and start the engine
Only start the engine: the helmet and lights will be checked after the start
questions.explain: Under the methodology the candidate puts on and fastens the helmet, adjusts the mirrors, takes a place in the pre-start zone, starts the engine and switches on the dipped headlight. Crossing the “Start” line without the dipped headlight or without the left indicator gives 10 penalty points for each.

questions.q: After the “Start” command you moved off only after 25 seconds. How many penalty points will be given?
questions.explain: Under the methodology you must move off within 20 seconds. A delay of more than 20 seconds gives 25 points, and if you do not start moving within 30 seconds, it is 100 points and the test is failed.

questions.q: What must you do before the “Finish” line at the category A test?
options: Switch on the left indicator
Switch on the right indicator
Sound the horn
Switch off the headlight
questions.explain: Before the finish line you switch on the right indicator, cross the line and stop the motorcycle. Not switching on the indicator before the line gives 10 penalty points.

questions.q: In the “Dimensional corridor” you ran a wheel over a control line once, but did not touch the ground with your foot. How many penalty points will you get?
questions.explain: Under the methodology, running a wheel over a control line gives 25 penalty points. The test is failed if the total is more than 99, so four such errors already mean failure.

questions.q: You want to obtain categories A and B at the same time. How will you take the tests?
options: Two theory tests and two practical tests: separately for each category
One theory test and one joint practical test in a car
Only the practical test: the theory test is not taken for A
One theory test and a separate practical test for each category
questions.explain: When obtaining a licence with several categories, the candidate takes one theory test and a practical test for each category separately. For A the practical test is taken on a two-wheeled motorcycle, and for B in a car.
